identity.name: Babylonia
alt_names: Dynasty IV of Babylon (Second Dynasty of Isin)

land.text: a tract of land around Babylon appropriated by Sumu-abum

predecessors.note: The Babylonia infobox lists "Sumer; Akkadian Empire" as predecessors without dates; the land was Akkad north of Isin and Larsa.

land.text: Babylonia restored as an independent kingdom by Nabopolassar

successors.note: Same state: the Chaldean dynasty. Cliopatria starts the Neo-Babylonian Empire in -600; this batch starts it with Nabopolassar's investiture in November 626 (Neo-Assyrian Empire page).

capitals.name: Babylon (near Hillah)
capitals.note: Infobox "Capital: Babylon", no years given. The Kassite court also used Dur-Kurigalzu (44.2 E 33.35 N), "Later rule shifted to the new city of Dur-Kurigalzu" (Kassites page). Babylon was sacked repeatedly and "destroyed" in 689 (Neo-Assyrian Empire page).

correction.text: the tract of land around Babylon (Dilbat, Sippar, Kisurra) of Sumu-abum and his successors

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first shape is -1800 but the page dates Babylonia from 1894 BC ("Around 1894 BC, an Amorite chieftain named Sumu-abum appropriated a tract of land"; the King of Babylon page: first king of Babylon). The page gives no extent; Cliopatria's 7,833 km2 is the best proxy.
7,833 km2: Hammurabi "ascended to the throne as the king of a minor kingdom"; his father "begun to consolidate rule of a small area of south central Mesopotamia". No infobox area on any page.

correction.text: the lower plain plus Eshnunna, the Euphrates up to Mari and the north, without Assur

keyframe_review.note: 97,099 km2 is the lower plain after the Larsa annexation (c. 1763: "the entirety of the lower Mesopotamian plain"). Hammurabi's northern conquests (Eshnunna "soon after", Mari, the region c. 1761 per the Old Assyrian period page, tribute from Assyria c. 1751) belong to these years, whereas Cliopatria adds them only in -1750. Corrected to the -1750 shape without the Assyrian core, which pays tribute but is not annexed.

correction.text: Hammurabi's kingdom without the Assyrian core; valid -1750..-1733

keyframe_review.note: 220,075 km2 at Hammurabi's height ("almost all of Mesopotamia"; a stele at Diyarbakir where he claims "King of the Amorites"), valid until Samsu-iluna loses Sumer in -1732. The Assur core is Assyria's own (tribute c. 1751), so it is cut out.

union.text: the Euphrates up to and including the ruins of Mari

correction.text: Akkad and the Euphrates to Mari

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -1732..-1701: after Ilum-ma-ili's Sealand takes the south ("the far south of Mesopotamia was lost", Babylonia page) Samsu-iluna "was left with a kingdom that was only fractionally larger than the one he started with", keeping "mastery of the Euphrates River up to and including the ruins of Mari". Akkad and the middle Euphrates; Cliopatria keeps all 220,075 km2 to -1701.

union.text: the marsh core at the head of the Gulf plus the Dhi-Qar and Basra governorates (Girsu, Lagash, Ur, Larsa), Uruk, Nippur and Isin: 'Sealand pottery has been found at Girsu, Uruk, and Lagash but in no site north of that'; Ilum-ma-ili 'is thought to have conquered Nippur late in Samsu-iluna's reign' (the corrected Sealand land of the window patches)
the desert of Al-Muthanna south of Ur and Uruk, which the Sealand's Dhi-Qar and Uruk cut off from Babylonia

correction.text: Babylonia without the Sealand-held south (the corrected Sealand land: Dhi-Qar, Basra, Uruk, Nippur and Isin, not the 42-50 E x 27-32.3 N rectangle) and without the Muthanna desert beyond it; the complement of first-sealand-dynasty_-1700 as the window patch m1700-m1601 draws it, as babylonia_-1600 and babylonia_-1500 are drawn in the patches m1600-m1501 and m1500-m1401

keyframe_review.note: 126,725 km2 (-1700..-1601) includes the south down to 30.3 N, but the Sealand dynasty held Sumer: Ilum-ma-ili "founded the First Dynasty of Sea-Land, which would remain in control of Sumer for the next 300 years" (Samsu-iluna) and Babylonia was "free of Babylon" for 272 years. Cut at 32.3 N, keeping Babylon (32.54 N) and cutting Nippur, Isin, Kisurra. R023 (3 Nov 2026): the rectangle cut at 32.3 N is replaced by the corrected Sealand land. First Sealand dynasty page: "Sealand pottery has been found at Girsu, Uruk, and Lagash but in no site north of that"; Ilum-ma-ili is "thought to have conquered Nippur late in Samsu-iluna's reign". The rectangle took Sumer north of the pottery sites (down to 27 N and across the whole 42-50 E strip) from Babylonia. (Source of the original keyframe: Samsu-iluna.)

minus.text: Sumer south of Nippur, held by the First Sealand dynasty

keyframe_review.note: 126,752 km2 (-1600..-1501): same correction as -1700; the Hittite sack (1595) and the Kassite takeover change the dynasty, not the shape.

minus.text: Sumer south of Nippur, held by the First Sealand dynasty until 1460

correction.text: Kassite Babylonia without the Sealand-held south; valid -1500..-1461

keyframe_review.note: 119,450 km2: valid without the south until the Sealand falls (-1460: "The fall of the First Sealand dynasty in 1460 BC created a power vacuum which the Kassites filled"; Ulamburiash "around 1450", Babylonia page; the Sealand page span ends c. 1475). Cut Sumer for -1500..-1461.

correction.text: Kassite Babylonia with the Sealand and Sumer

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -1460..-1401: Kassite Babylonia with the former Sealand and Sumer incorporated ("Ulam-Buriaš conquered the Sealand, incorporated it into Babylonia", Sealand page). This is Cliopatria's -1500 shape with Sumer, i.e. the full 119,450 km2.

226,484 km2 (maximum): Kurigalzu I "conquered Elam and sacked the capital of Susa" (mid 14th century) and Kassite power "into the Persian Gulf, including at Qal'at al-Bahrain" (Agum III tablets). Pages give no area or frontier; the bbox to Kuwait and to 35.6 N is Cliopatria's.

155,212 km2: Kurigalzu II (c. 1332-1308) and the Sugagi war: the Synchronistic Chronicle says Assyria and Babylonia "divided the districts from Šasili of Subartu, to Karduniaš into two and fixed the boundary-line", perhaps "a loss of territory from Assyria to Babylon". The line is not on the page.
134,294 km2 (-1240..-1221). From c. 1225 Babylonia was Tukulti-Ninurta I's vassal until c. 1216 (assyria dossier); the shape stays Babylonia's own land, drawn lighter under the vassal events.

correction.text: Kassite Babylonia, vassal of Assyria to c. 1216

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -1220..-1201: Cliopatria has no Babylonia shape here because its Assyria shape swallows it. Tukulti-Ninurta I held Babylonia only c. 1225-1216; Adad-shuma-usur drove the Assyrians out c. 1216 and the Kassite dynasty ruled to 1155 (Babylonia page).

132,636 km2 (-1200..-1151) is valid until the Kassite dynasty ends: "lasting until 1155 BC, when Babylon was conquered by Shutruk-Nakhunte of Elam". Elam holds Babylonia from 1155 (the elam dossier: 1158-1153); the next keyframe restores it.

correction.text: Babylonia under the Second Dynasty of Isin

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -1153..-1101: Cliopatria has no shape -1150..-1101 although "Marduk-kabit-ahheshu (1155-1139 BC)" founds Dynasty IV of Babylon, from Isin, and Nebuchadnezzar I rules c. 1121-1100. The land is the Kassite shape.

132,636 km2 (-1100..-1001), identical to -1200. Nebuchadnezzar I "is titled as the conqueror of the Amorite lands" and "despoiler of the Kassites"; the page names no land gained or lost, and "No contemporary or later source records a sack of Susa by Nebuchadnezzar". Unverified in detail.
25,192 km2 core: Nabu-shum-libur's dynasty was "deposed by marauding Arameans in 1026 BC" and Arameans and Suteans settled Babylonia "during the 11th century BC"; the page gives no land lost.

118,948 km2: Adad-nirari II "managed to secure a border agreement with the Babylonian king Nabu-shuma-ukin I"; "By 850 BC the migrant Chaldeans had established a small territory" (Babylonia page). Cliopatria's regrowth from 25 k to 119 k km2 is not on a page.

correction.text: Babylonia between Shamshi-Adad V and Tiglath-Pileser III

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -800..-730: Cliopatria has no Babylonia shape, its Neo-Assyrian shapes covering the north, but the pages show Babylon with kings of its own until Tiglath-Pileser III "in 729 BC ... decided to rule Babylon directly". Extent assumed equal to -900 (page silent, unverified).
New keyframe -721..-711: "Marduk-apla-iddina managed to take the throne of Babylon itself between 721 and 710 BC".

133,938 km2 (-650..-631): the Babylonian kingdom of Shamash-shum-ukin's revolt (652-648) and the Assyrian vassal kings after Ashurbanipal "captured Babylon after a long siege" in 648; the page does not name Kandalanu. The shape lies inside Cliopatria's Neo-Assyrian shape.

correction.text: Babylonia under Assyrian-appointed kings until Nov. 626

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -630..-626: Cliopatria has no shape for the last Assyrian years of Babylonia; the same land until Nabopolassar, "formally invested as king of Babylon in November 626 BCE, restoring Babylonia as an independent kingdom".

correction.text: unchanged but assigned to neo-babylonian-empire from -626

keyframe_review.note: 152,403 km2 for -615..-601 belongs to the Neo-Babylonian Empire (founded 626) in the neo-babylonian-empire dossier; Babylonia ends in -626 here.

region.text: a tract of land around Babylon

ledger.note: 1894 BC: Sumu-abum founds Babylon's First Dynasty. "Around 1894 BC, an Amorite chieftain named Sumu-abum appropriated a tract of land" (infobox "Established: 1894 BC"); the King of Babylon page: "Sumu-abum was the first king of Babylon". The page gives no boundary.

region.text: Larsa (Tell as-Senkereh), besieged for six months

ledger.note: c. 1764 BC: Hammurabi turns on Larsa. "Around 1764 BC, Hammurabi turned against Rim-Sin, who had refused to support Hammurabi in his war against Elam despite pledging his troops." Mirrors larsa.

region.text: Larsa

ledger.note: c. 1763 BC: the siege ends. "Hammurabi's forces quickly reached Larsa, and after a six-month siege the city fell." The page dates Rim-Sin's death "c. 1763 BC"; the annexation follows in the next event. Mirrors larsa.

region.text: the entirety of the lower Mesopotamian plain

ledger.note: c. 1763 BC: Hammurabi annexes Larsa and the whole lower plain. "Hammurabi invaded and then annexed Larsa, thus gaining control of the entirety of the lower Mesopotamian plain around 1763 BC."

region.text: Eshnunna and its kingdom: the Diyala, Arrapha and Rapiqum lands

ledger.note: 1762 BC (Hammurabi year 31): Babylon occupies Eshnunna. The Eshnunna page: "the Babylonians occupied the city of Eshnunna" in "Year 31 of Hammurabi" (1762 BC); the Hammurabi page has the destruction of Eshnunna "soon after" Larsa. The region is the eshnunna dossier's last extent, drawn from names (Diyala, Kirkuk, Euphrates circle).

region.text: the kingdom of Mari: the Euphrates valley, Suhum and the Upper Khabur

ledger.note: c. 1761 BC: Babylon ends the Lim dynasty of Mari. "Babylon invaded in c. 1761 BC under the rule of Hammurabi and defeated Zimri-Lin, ending the Lim dynasty"; Terqa then "became the capital of the rump Kingdom of Hana" and "the Suhum region became a Babylonian province". The Hammurabi page: "conquered the remaining northern states, including Babylon's former ally Mari, although it is possible that the conquest of Mari was a surrender without any actual conflict". The region is the lim-dynasty-of-mari dossier's last extent; the Hana rump at Terqa is not carved out (page gives no frontier).

region.text: Assur and its core

ledger.note: c. 1751 BC: Assyria pays tribute. Hammurabi "forced their successor Mut-Ashkur to pay tribute to Babylon c. 1751 BC"; the Old Assyrian period page adds that Hammurabi "appears to have respected Assur and its institutions".

region.text: the far south: Uruk, Ur, Isin, Kisurra and the rest of Sumer

ledger.note: c. 1732-1721 BC: Sumer secedes under Ilum-ma-ili. "A few years later, a pretender calling himself Ilum-ma-ili" raised "another pan-Sumerian revolt", dated "between the 18th and 29th year of Samsu-iluna's reign" (accession 1749, middle chronology: 1732-1721); he "founded the First Dynasty of Sea-Land". The Rim-Sin II revolt of year 9 (1741) spread to 26 cities but was put down when "Larsa itself was defeated".

region.text: Assur and its core

ledger.note: By the end of Samsu-iluna's reign (1712) Assyria is free: Puzur-Sin "ejected Asinum", Adasi "restored a stable native dynasty" removing "any vestages of Amorite-Babylonian influence"; the page gives no year and says Samsu-iluna "seems to have been powerless to intervene".

region.text: the middle Euphrates down to Mari

ledger.note: Cliopatria's -1700 shape no longer reaches the Euphrates or Mari (west edge 43.4 E). Samsu-iluna had "mastery of the Euphrates River up to and including the ruins of Mari"; no page dates the loss.

1595 BC: the Hittites sack Babylon and the Kassites take the throne. "Babylon was then attacked by the Indo-European-speaking, Anatolia-based Hittites in 1595 BC" and "Agum II took the throne for the Kassites in 1595 BC"; "It is not clear precisely when Kassite rule of Babylon began", and the Kassites page has "c. 1531 BC until c. 1155 BC". Same state, same colour (rule 2): the Kassite dynasty is recorded as Karduniaš, not as a separate state.

region.text: the Sealand incorporated into Babylonia: its corrected land (marsh core, Dhi-Qar and Basra governorates, Uruk, Nippur, Isin), not the rectangle: Ulam-Buriash 'conquered the Sealand' and 'incorporated it into Babylonia'

ledger.note: c. 1460 BC: the Kassites absorb the Sealand and Sumer. "The fall of the First Sealand dynasty in 1460 BC created a power vacuum which the Kassites filled"; the Babylonia page dates Ulamburiash's attack "around 1450 BC" and the Sealand page ends the dynasty c. 1475. R023 (3 Nov 2026): region changed from the 42-50 E x 27-32.3 N rectangle to the corrected Sealand land (the one the patches m1500-m1401 and m1600-m1501 give first-sealand-dynasty), which includes Nippur's disc that the rectangle left at 32.3 N. First Sealand dynasty page: Ea-gamil, the last king, fled to Elam before an army led by the Kassite chief Ulam-Buriash, who "conquered the Sealand" and "incorporated it into Babylonia" (the page dates only the dynasty, c. 1732-1475 BC (MC), not the conquest).

region.text: the Kassite additions of Cliopatria's -1400 shape; the page names only the Gulf (Dilmun)

ledger.note: Cliopatria widens the shape at -1400 to 226,484 km2 (north to 35.6 N, west to 40 E, south to Kuwait). Kurigalzu I reigned "(1415-1390 BC)" (Babylonia page) and the Kassites "extended their power into the Persian Gulf, including at Qal'at al-Bahrain"; no page gives the land.

region.text: Elam, with its capital Susa

ledger.note: Mid 14th century BC: Kurigalzu I invades Elam. "under Kurigalzu I in the mid 14th century BC, conquered Elam and sacked the capital of Susa". The Kurigalzu II page: the Elam conquest "now tends to be assigned to the earlier king of this name" (the elam dossier has Kurigalzu II c. 1320).

region.text: Elam, with its capital Susa

ledger.note: The page gives no duration; the occupation of Elam is closed one year after it began (the elam dossier calls the Kassite occupation temporary).

region.text: Babylonia, carried off by Elam

ledger.note: 1155 BC: Shutruk-Nakhunte ends the Kassite dynasty. "lasting until 1155 BC, when Babylon was conquered by Shutruk-Nakhunte of Elam" (the Kassites page: the last king "was taken to Susa and imprisoned there in 1155 BC", "an unreliable account"); the elam dossier has the conquest in 1158, and the Babylonia page already lists Marduk-kabit-ahheshu from 1155.

region.text: Babylonia under Dynasty IV from Isin

ledger.note: Babylonia returns under the Second Dynasty of Isin. The Babylonia page lists "Marduk-kabit-ahheshu (1155-1139 BC)" and gives no Elamite occupation; -1153 follows the elam dossier (page silent).

region.text: Babylonia outside its core, overrun by Arameans and Suteans

ledger.note: Babylonia shrinks to its core in Cliopatria's -1000 shape. Nabu-shum-libur's dynasty "deposed by marauding Arameans in 1026 BC"; Arameans and Suteans settled Babylonia "during the 11th century BC". The pages date the Aramean arrival, not the land lost; -1000 is Cliopatria's year.

region.text: the land Babylonia holds again by the border agreement with Assyria; no page names it

ledger.note: Cliopatria regrows the shape in -900 to 118,948 km2. Adad-nirari II "managed to secure a border agreement with the Babylonian king Nabu-shuma-ukin I" and Chaldeans were settled by 850; the pages date no recovery of land.

region.text: Babylonia, ruled directly by the Assyrian king

ledger.note: 729 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III takes Babylon. "In 729 BCE, he captured Babylon, defeated Nabu-mukin-zēri" (Neo-Assyrian Empire page); the Babylonia page: he "decided to rule Babylon directly".

region.text: Babylonia under Marduk-apla-iddina

ledger.note: 721-710 BC: Marduk-apla-iddina holds Babylon. "Marduk-apla-iddina managed to take the throne of Babylon itself between 721 and 710 BC." The page gives the span, not the year of the seizure.

region.text: Babylonia, ruled again by the Assyrian king

ledger.note: 710 BC: Sargon II retakes Babylon. "When Sargon marched south in 710 BCE he encountered little resistance."

region.text: Babylonia with a king of its own

ledger.note: Babylon has a king of its own again by 652 (Shamash-shum-ukin revolts "in 652 BCE"); the pages give no date for the end of direct Assyrian rule or for Sennacherib's and Esarhaddon's arrangements ("Babylon was destroyed" in 689). Placed one year before the revolt.

region.text: Babylonia and its Elamite allies against Ashurbanipal

ledger.note: 652 BC: Shamash-shum-ukin revolts at Babylon. "in 652 BCE he revolted with the aid of several Elamite kings."

region.text: Babylonia

ledger.note: 648 BC: Ashurbanipal takes Babylon. "In 648 BCE Ashurbanipal captured Babylon after a long siege." Babylonia stays a separate kingdom under an Assyrian-appointed king (vassal events in the neo-assyrian-empire dossier).

region.text: Babylonia, independent again

ledger.note: Nov. 626 BC: Nabopolassar founds the Chaldean (Neo-Babylonian) dynasty. "Nabopolassar was formally invested as king of Babylon in November 626 BCE, restoring Babylonia as an independent kingdom." Same state, new dynasty; the neo-babylonian-empire dossier continues the land.

wars.name: Hammurabi's conquest of Larsa
wars.outcome: Hammurabi annexed Larsa around 1763 and gained "the entirety of the lower Mesopotamian plain"; Rim-Sin I was Hammurabi's earlier ally.

wars.name: Hammurabi's northern campaigns

zones.text: Eshnunna, Mari and the northern states

wars.outcome: "Soon after" Larsa he destroyed Eshnunna and his armies took the northern states including Mari (possibly a surrender); Mut-Ashkur of Assyria paid tribute c. 1751.
wars.note: The page dates none of these but Larsa and the tribute.

wars.name: Revolt of Rim-Sin II

zones.text: the southern cities that joined the revolt

wars.outcome: In the ninth year of Samsu-iluna a man calling himself Rim-Sin raised a revolt that "spread to include some 26 cities"; he was killed when "Larsa itself was defeated". Uruk and Ur records stop after year 10.
wars.note: Years computed from accession 1749 (middle chronology); the page gives regnal years only. In the same year (9) Samsu-iluna "turned back an invasion by a Kassite army", the earliest mention of the Kassites.

wars.name: Ilum-ma-ili's revolt and the First Sealand dynasty
wars.outcome: Ilum-ma-ili's pan-Sumerian revolt "founded the First Dynasty of Sea-Land"; by Samsu-iluna's death "Nippur recognized Ilum-ma-ili as king". Sumer stayed outside Babylonia for 272-300 years.
wars.note: Years are regnal years 18-29 converted from 1749; "very uncertain".

wars.name: Hittite sack of Babylon
wars.outcome: "Babylon was then attacked by the Indo-European-speaking, Anatolia-based Hittites in 1595 BC"; no land passed to Hatti. Agum II took the throne for the Kassites in the same year per the page.

wars.name: Kassite conquest of the Sealand
wars.outcome: Ulam-Buriash "conquered the Sealand, incorporated it into Babylonia"; Agum III attacked it again, destroying a temple in Dur-Enlil.
wars.note: Pages differ: fall in 1460 (Kassites), Ulamburiash "around 1450 BC" (Babylonia), dynasty to c. 1475 (Sealand).

wars.name: Assyrian intervention under Ashur-uballit I
wars.outcome: "in 1333 BC, a usurper named Nazi-Bugaš deposed him [Kara-hardash], enraging Ashur-uballit I, who invaded and sacked Babylon"; Kurigalzu II was placed on the Kassite throne.
wars.note: The Kurigalzu II page also says he was placed by Ashur-uballit I; no year there.

wars.name: Kurigalzu II and Enlil-nirari at Sugagi

zones.text: the districts "from Šasili of Subartu, to Karduniaš" divided at the boundary-line

wars.outcome: The Synchronistic Chronicle: the kings "divided the districts from Šasili of Subartu, to Karduniaš into two and fixed the boundary-line"; the epic texts "may perhaps suggest an indecisive outcome".
wars.note: Years are Enlil-nirari's reign (c. 1327-1318, Middle Assyrian Empire page); the Kurigalzu II page gives no year for the battle.

wars.name: Tukulti-Ninurta I's conquest of Babylonia
wars.outcome: "the Assyrian king Tukulti-Ninurta I (1243-1207 BC) routed his armies, sacked and burned Babylon"; Kashtiliash IV was deposed c. 1225. Babylonia was an Assyrian vassal until c. 1216.

wars.name: Elamite conquest of Babylonia
wars.outcome: Shutruk-Nakhunte conquered Babylon and carried off the Statue of Marduk; the Kassite dynasty ended.

wars.name: Nebuchadnezzar I's war with Elam
wars.outcome: Nebuchadnezzar I "routed the Elamite king Ḫulteludiš-Inšušinak on the banks of the river Ulaya" and recovered the statue of Marduk in a surprise summer attack from Der; "No contemporary or later source records a sack of Susa". He also fought Ashur-resh-ishi I at Zanqi and Idi.
wars.note: "The duration of Nebuchadnezzar's war with Elam and the number of campaigns he conducted are not known": years are his reign.

wars.name: Shalmaneser III in Babylonia
wars.outcome: Shalmaneser III, "in 851-850 BCE, aided the Babylonian king Marduk-zakir-shumi I to defeat a revolt by his brother"; the Babylonia page says he "sacked Babylon itself" (859-824).

wars.name: Shamshi-Adad V against Marduk-balassu-iqbi
wars.outcome: "In 813 BCE, he defeated Marduk-balassu-iqbi and brought him to Assyria as a captive."

wars.name: Tiglath-Pileser III's conquest of Babylon
wars.outcome: "In 729 BCE, he captured Babylon, defeated Nabu-mukin-zēri"; he ruled Babylon directly.

wars.name: Sargon II's Babylonian campaign
wars.outcome: Sargon "encountered little resistance" in 710 and displaced Marduk-apla-iddina.
wars.note: Marduk-apla-iddina held the throne "between 721 and 710 BC" (Babylonia page).

wars.name: Revolt of Shamash-shum-ukin
wars.outcome: Shamash-shum-ukin revolted in 652 with Elamite help; Ashurbanipal captured Babylon after a long siege in 648.

certainty.note: Ancient frontiers are approximate throughout. The Assyria-Babylonia boundary "fixed" after Sugagi under Kurigalzu II is the only line the pages mention, and not even its course is given.
Last year of the state; the Neo-Babylonian Empire continues it.

notes:
SPLIT AND SCOPE. Cliopatria's Babylonia row (-1800..-601) is one state: Old Babylonian (Amorite) -> Kassite (rename -1595) -> Second Dynasty of Isin and the Aramean/Chaldean centuries -> Assyrian rule -> Nabopolassar, who founds the Neo-Babylonian Empire dossier. The orchestrator scope calls for the Kassite dynasty as a separate state; rule 2 (a dynasty on the same land without a break stays in the state) and the Babylonia article (one kingdom 1894-539 BC) decided against it, so the Kassites are a rename, not a dossier. If the colour agent wants Kassite Babylonia in its own colour, split at -1595 and -1153 (the shapes babylonia_-1600..-1460 and the new keyframes already break there). The dossier ends in Nov. -626 with the Neo-Babylonian start, 25 years before Cliopatria's row end; the shape babylonia_-615 is marked wrong for this slug.
